correctness.rationale: For X=G∘K1 with n>=2, D dominates iff D intersects every private core/leaf pair (because each leaf has only its core neighbor). For any partition, this translates coalition partners into 2-vertex covers of the labeled block-incidence multigraph; there are no singleton dominating vertices. If k>=5, choosing cover {a,b} leaves >=3 vertices in independent remainder; at least one cover vertex has >=2 neighbors in that remainder, forcing all other vertices covers with it, which would make it a forbidden one-cover. For k=4, cover combinatorics exclude loops and characterize exactly 2K2, P4, C4 supports. Surjective assignment of each labeled private pair to an abstract support edge with two orientations and free quotient by automorphisms 8,2,8 gives Nn=2^(n-3)(4^n-5·2^n+6). Independently enumerated all set partitions for n=2,3,4 (respectively 15,203,4140 Bell cases) checking raw incidence coalition predicate; maxima k4 counts 1,30,364 agree. Infinite statement rests on cover proof, not finite census.
residual_risks: The original bundled n=5 exhaustive claim was not rerun; independent n<=4 checks plus complete mathematical argument suffice for arbitrary n.
Partitions are of labeled vertices, unordered blocks, not mod graph automorphisms.

originality.rationale: Ordinary coalition number and coalition partner structures differ from connected coalition number CC(G∘K1)=2 known in connected-corona work. The 2021 tree coalition paper handles extremal tree thresholds and coalition graphs of paths, not all core graphs or unlabeled support-orbit enumerations. The recent May 2026 coalition-count note computes the maximum number of coalition partners in a partition, not the number of maximum partitions; its full eight-page paper contains no corona claim. The 2026 k-coalition preprint assumes k>=2, so its corona cases do not settle ordinary k=1. Resultary leaf-corona superdomination count is different invariant. No primary inspected source implies the universal all-G C=4 and Nn.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact ordinary-coalition corona theorem may exist; none found among targeted current published statements.

value.rationale: A corona operation makes ordinary domination wholly private-pair-local, unexpectedly erasing all dependence on base edges. This yields a natural complete optimal-partition classification and exact exponential count for every base graph; the incidence types and count distinguish ordinary versus connected coalitions and are independently useful graph-partition invariants.
residual_risks: Not a classification of coalition partitions of non-leaf coronas; no graph-automorphism orbit count.

limitations: n>=2 and exactly one private leaf per core vertex, arbitrary G simple, possibly disconnected.
Direct independent exhaustive counts stop at n4, and no independent census n5; all-n follows a combinatorial proof.
